zones.name: Panchajanya Brass Aarti Ghanta & Shankha Bell (teaching replica)
zones.title: Mangal Aarti and the temple beginnings
lines: At Puri in Odisha, the present Shree Jagannath Temple began under King Anantavarman Chodaganga Deva of the Eastern Ganga dynasty in the twelfth century.
This bell and conch recall Mangal Aarti, the early morning worship of Jagannath. Their sound calls attention to prayer and the daily service that keeps the temple tradition alive.
Temple tradition also tells of King Indradyumna and sacred timber. That is a cherished foundation legend, distinct from the documented history of the present stone temple.
choices: How do we protect this craft?
zones.extra: Legends express devotion and community identity. Historical claims use inscriptions and other evidence; both deserve careful explanation.
zones.care: Keep replicas documented and handle them carefully. Real sacred objects remain in the care of their community.
zones.aryan: I have recovered the bell and conch teaching replica.

zones.name: Tala-Patra Gita Govinda Palm-Leaf Manuscript (teaching replica)
zones.title: Palm-leaf writing and Gita Govinda
lines: This palm-leaf manuscript recalls tala patra, an Odisha craft that preserves writing and pictures on prepared palm leaves. Artists incise fine lines with a stylus and darken them with pigment.
The Gita Govinda was composed by the twelfth-century poet Jayadeva. Its devotional verses are sung in Jagannath worship, connecting poetry, music and temple service.
Preserving a manuscript protects more than words. It keeps a language, an artist's skill and generations of community memory available to the people who come after us.
choices: How do we care for this replica?
zones.extra: Manuscripts preserve language, poetry and the knowledge of their makers. Real leaves are fragile and need trained conservation rather than a quick repair.
zones.care: Keep replicas documented and handle them carefully. Real sacred objects remain in the care of their community.
zones.aryan: I have recovered the palm-leaf teaching manuscript.

zones.name: Ashtadhatu Nilachakra Seal & Pattachitra Medallion (teaching replica)
zones.title: Nilachakra and Pattachitra craftsmanship
lines: The Nilachakra is the sacred wheel above the Shree Jagannath Temple at Puri. It is made from ashtadhatu, an alloy traditionally described as eight metals.
The temple flag is associated with this wheel. The small seal you recovered recalls that landmark; the actual sacred wheel remains on the temple.
Pattachitra is Odisha's detailed story-painting tradition. Artists use careful outlines and prepared colours to preserve devotional stories, including stories associated with Jagannath.
choices: How do we protect this craft?
zones.extra: Pattachitra carries stories through line, colour and patient workshop practice. Supporting practising artists helps skills pass between generations.
zones.care: Keep replicas documented and handle them carefully. Real sacred objects remain in the care of their community.
zones.aryan: I have recovered the wheel seal and painted teaching medallion.

zones.name: Abadha Kumbha & Rohini Kunda Brass Kalasha (teaching replica)
zones.title: Mahaprasad and water traditions
lines: This vessel introduces Mahaprasad, the sacred food offered at Shree Jagannath Temple. The temple kitchen prepares offerings in earthen pots through the skilled service of its cooks.
Rohini Kunda is a sacred water place within the temple tradition. A water vessel can help us remember the place of water, offerings and daily care in worship.
Nirmalya includes dried sacred rice cherished by devotees. Food traditions remind us that heritage lives through people who prepare, share and care for it, as well as through buildings.
choices: Why discuss the people behind offerings?
How do we care for this replica?
zones.extra: Living heritage includes the people who maintain a tradition. We honour their knowledge and work, and avoid treating sacred food as treasure or a commodity.
zones.care: Keep replicas documented and handle them carefully. Real sacred objects remain in the care of their community.
zones.aryan: I have recovered the ceremonial teaching vessel.

zones.name: Nandighosha Chariot Wheel Medallion & Ratha Pataka (teaching replica)
zones.title: Ratha Yatra and the chariot makers
lines: Ratha Yatra is the great chariot festival of Puri. Jagannath, Balabhadra and Subhadra travel along Bada Danda, the Grand Avenue, towards Gundicha Temple.
Jagannath's chariot is Nandighosha, with sixteen wheels. Balabhadra's is Taladhwaja and Subhadra's is Darpadalana. Each chariot has its own established design.
Skilled carpenters build the chariots anew each year. The wheel and banner recall a living tradition in which making, devotion and community participation carry knowledge forward.
choices: How do we protect this craft?
zones.extra: Rebuilding keeps specialist skills alive through practice and transmission. The knowledge of the makers matters as much as the finished woodwork.
zones.care: Keep replicas documented and handle them carefully. Real sacred objects remain in the care of their community.
zones.aryan: I have recovered the chariot teaching medallion and banner.

zones.name: Shree Mandir Swarna Kalasha & Daru Brahma Chronicle Ornament (teaching replica)
zones.title: Living heritage and Nabakalebara
lines: A kalasha is a crowning vessel form in temple architecture. This finial ornament helps us notice how the upper parts of a temple contribute to its identity and craftsmanship.
At Puri, Nabakalebara is the periodic renewal of the sacred wooden images in the Jagannath tradition. The images are associated with sacred neem wood, or daru.
This is why heritage is more than the price of wood or metal. People preserve and renew its meaning through knowledge, care and worship. Protecting heritage means protecting living community memory.
choices: How do we care for this replica?
zones.extra: People renew heritage through knowledge, care and shared responsibility. Every temple holds a story; protecting heritage means protecting our history.
zones.care: Keep replicas documented and handle them carefully. Real sacred objects remain in the care of their community.
zones.aryan: I have recovered the teaching finial and chronicle ornament.
